transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 1:12
Attendees: Elliot Shaw, Maya Chen, Priya Patel, Tomás Rivera, Kofi Mensah, Lena Ortiz, Samir Gupta + All hands
Link: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/velocity-briefing-nov2026

00:00 Elliot Shaw (CEO): okay, welcome everyone, uh thanks for joining on the Tuesday morning all hands. quick signal, this is a, like, shorter than usual leadership briefing, we want to focus on operations and the things we need to lock before the holidays. um i'll hand it to maya for a quick runtime update then priya on product.
00:27 Maya Chen (CTO): thanks elliot. quick highlights — servr runtime updates are in. note i said servr, uh service runtime, i— the team just pushed the attention kernel changes and we see about 18% token cost reduction on the Llama-family workloads in our internal bench. fuzz in transcription there sorry. also we're close on continuous batching improvements; latency tail is down but there are still spikes when cache misses happen.
01:05 Priya Patel (VP Product): i'll show the roadmap slide — Optimize v2 will land in two weeks for early beta customers. main things: (a) smarter prefix caching heuristics; (b) model switching by cost-per-token fuzzy logic; (c) pre-warming for scheduled batch jobs. beta target: 5 production customers, we already have 3 signed up from the pilot program.
01:40 Tomás Rivera (Head of Infra): on infra, we rolled a region-specific failover policy last week; it operates as an earlier circuit breaker for cross-region routing. caught a weird quirk where KV cash was being flushed incorrectly — yes i said cash not cache — that caused some small blips in europe. Kofi is doing the postmortem.
02:05 Kofi Mensah (Head of SRE): thanks tomás. quick postmortem summary: on 10/28 we saw a spike due to an orchestration race during autoscale; reconciliation loop failed to rehydrate some kv cache entries and requests fell back to hosted heavier model causing latency and cost jump. root cause: timing window in scale controller + a metric aggregation bug. impact window ~ 18 minutes. action: runbook v3 with explicit reconciliation checks, add a canary under high churn, and a new alert for backing-off on model fallback. i'll publish the runbook by next Tuesday.
03:02 Elliot: that's helpful. small ask — can we get a short one-pager for sales to explain the rollback/fallback behavior? lena — can you take that?
03:15 Lena Ortiz (Head of Sales): yep we can, we'll craft an FAQ: dedicated vs hosted, what fallback means for SLAs, and how burst capacity is billed. also note: we've had pushback from a few EMEA accounts about data residency for private deployments.
03:34 Samir Gupta (Head Eng Ops): hiring update: we've converted three contractor roles to full time for infra and SRE; however, we are pausing non-critical open roles for this quarter to focus on finish line delivery. compensation cycles remain on schedule.
03:58 Audience (misc questions): (Speaker 3): will there be a freeze on hiring for sales as well? (Lena): no freeze for quota-critical sellers, just slow down on support roles.
04:18 Priya: product risks — two big items: tokenizer drift on some third-party models and the plan to add model-specific quant profiles. we're turning up a canary to validate quality metrics against our eval sets.
04:44 Maya: on the latency vs cost tradeoff — Optimize v2 will allow routing policies based on a new delta metric: expected cost per effective token. it can route to a cheaper quantized variant when the downstream quality regression is within a defined threshold. tradeoffs are subtle and we will need customer sign-off for defaults.
05:15 Elliot: okay, high level — we need to be transparent in docs and in console defaults. customers shouldn't be surprised by quiet model swaps.
05:30 Q&A (live):
05:31 Speaker 5: uh, any update on SOC2 scope expansion? (Priya): yes we plan to include Dedicated pools in scope next quarter; security team will send the audit plan.
05:48 Speaker 6: are we changing pricing? (Elliot): no broad changes today. we are adjusting burst billing clarifications and will publish examples.
06:05 Priya: Optimize v2 launch plan — phased: internal beta -> pilot customers -> GA. feature flags will be exposed in console; default is conservative.
06:23 Tomás: tabletop drills — SRE+infra will run two tabletop incident drills in November, signups will open this week.
06:36 Kofi: and a note on runbooks — the new runbook emphasizes graceful fallback to model variant, how to escalate, and required post-incident review timeline.
06:52 Audience question: how about regional private availability? (Maya): we are opening APAC private region in December for a small set of customers; it's gated on KMS attestation and network egress controls. more on the private deployment page.
07:18 Elliot: ok now a very quick wins and wins section — kudos to the infra team for the kernel work; ops for stabilizing dashboards; sales for closing a mid-market deal last week.
07:33 Lightning demo (Priya): short demo of Optimize v2 UI — shows policy editor, quality sliders, and simulation tab. (screen share note: folks, there was a tiny lag). demo shows how a policy routes requests to smaller quantized model when quality delta < 2%.
08:40 Open Q&A — live questions about roadmap, quotas, and support. some cross talk, a couple of mics open.
10:12 Elliot: wrap-up — quick recap: publish deck, runbook v3, tabletop drills, sales FAQ, and finalize beta invites. we'll follow up with a short survey about topics for next leadership briefing.
10:30 Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions had occasional name errors and merged short sentences. There is some background noise during the demo.
